newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ageing Mexico union boss may take leave of absence.
newsitem.headline: Ageing Mexico union boss may take leave of absence.

text.p: Veteran union boss Fidel Velazquez, a key ally of the government for more than half a century, returned to work Monday after more than a month sick and said he might take a leave of absence soon.
Asked whether he would agree to being temporarily relieved of his duties as secretary-general of the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), the 97-year-old Velazquez said: "I accept it".
But he added that CTM oficials had been unwilling so far to allow him any leave of absence. "They are asking that I be the only person who can run the CTM", he added.
Various people including Juan S. Millan, secretary-general of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) have been mentioned as possible successors to Velazquez in his delicate job.
The CTM chief hinted that he favoured current first secretary Leonardo Rodriguez Alcaine but added that "it is forbidden to signal a preference for anyone".
